correctness.rationale: The Haar-normalized tent functions concentrate at the identity. The correlation formula uses only right invariance to bound the Lipschitz seminorm. For the Fourier convention used here, convolution multiplies matrices in order, and the involution becomes adjoint. Each correlation has positive semidefinite blocks, and on any fixed irreducible block all sufficiently late tents have invertible transforms; their positively weighted sum is therefore strictly positive definite on that block. Peter–Weyl gives injectivity without a uniform inverse bound. The kernel is a Lipschitz probability density; rewriting the integral with k(xb^{-1}) gives the stated Lipschitz bound after subtracting constants. Left convolution commutes with right shifts. The Jaworski–Chen observable embedding, shrunk around 1/2 and composed with Q, stays in [0,1], is 1-Lipschitz, and is still equivariant and injective. Compactness and the uniform topology give a topological embedding. The shift-fixed functions are precisely the constants. Connectedness enters only through the continuous embedding theorem.
residual_risks: No extension of the embedding criterion to disconnected groups or to noncompact non-Lie groups was checked or is implied.
